header.running_head: The Hijrah of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

blocks.text: accompany me.' I swear by Allaah that before then I had never known anyone to cry out of joy until I saw Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) cry that day. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, 'O Nabi of Allaah ﷺ! I have kept those two camels ready for this purpose.' He then hired Abdullaah bin Urayqidh as a guide to show them the way. He was a Mushrik from the Bahu Du'il bin Bakr tribe whose mother belonged to the Banu Sahm bin Amr tribe. They gave him their two camels and he kept them and grazed them until the appointed day." [^1]

A reliable narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) states that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked Rasulullaah ﷺ whether he could accompany him and Rasulullaah ﷺ agreed, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "I have two camel that I have fed for the past six months for this purpose. Take any one of the two." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I shall rather buy it." Rasulullaah ﷺ then bought the camel from Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and they both left. They then stayed in the cave. [^2]

Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) who was the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that that when they were staying in Makkah Rasulullaah ﷺ usually visited them twice each day. However, one day he arrived in the afternoon. She said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "Father, here comes Rasulullaah ﷺ. May my parents be sacrificed! It must be something important that has brought him at this hour." Rasulullaah ﷺ came and said, "Do you know that Allaah has permitted me to leave Makkah?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked, "May I accompany you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ?" "Certainly," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "I have two camels that I have been rearing from a long time in anticipation for this day. You may take one." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Only at a price, Abu Bakr." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! You may have it at a price if you so wish."
Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) says, "We then prepared the food for their journey. I cut my belt and used part of it to fasten their provisions." Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then left and stayed in a cave in the Thowr mountain. When they arrived at the cave, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) entered first and placed his finger in every hole, fearing that there may be an insect there (which would harm Rasulullaah ﷺ). When the Quraysh found out that they were gone, they set out in search of them and fixed a reward of a hundred camels for anyone who captured Rasulullaah ﷺ. They scoured the mountains of Makkah and eventually reached the mountain where Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) were hiding. Referring to a person who was facing the cave, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! He will surely see us." "Never," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ, "because the angels are hiding us with their wings." Still facing the cave, the man then sat down to pass urine. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Had he seen us, he would never have done that."
They stayed three nights in the cave and every evening Hadhrat Aamir bin Fuhayra (RA) would bring the goats of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) to them. At
Baghawi. The complete narration appears in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.334).
